newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kidnapped Austrian, five others freed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped Austrian, five others freed in Chechnya.

text.p: Rebels have freed an Austrian businessman and five others held hostage in the breakaway Russian region of Chechnya, Interfax news agency reported on Monday.
The release came as police in the rebel North Caucasus region stepped up efforts to counter a wave of kidnappings that has gripped Chechnya in recent months.

A political officer at the Austrian embassy in Moscow confirmed an Austrian had been released but could not provide details. RIA news agency named him as Robert Heel, and said he had been seized on April 2.
As part of the operation, Chechen authorities are blocking all roads leading into the region and checking cars, RIA said.
The kidnappings have undermined Chechnya's efforts to restore order and stability since a peace deal last August put an end to 21 months of war between pro-independence rebels and Russian troops.
Chechnya's President Aslan Maskhadov late last month offered a reward of $100,000 for information on the whereabouts of seven Russian journalists still held hostage.
Earlier in May, Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Maskhadov signed a peace accord promising to end centuries of conflict between Moscow and the Chechens.
Chechen Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov was expected in Moscow on Tuesday to continue talks on the peace process, Interfax reported.
